name: Public telegraph service in colonial India
summary: From 1855 telegraph offices in British colonial India offered message service to the public, letting ordinary people send fast long-distance messages.
description: Telegraph offices offering message service to the public in British colonial India.
tier_reason: A specific community-facing use or availability in electrical communication, power or computing.

impact.note: Brought fast long-distance messaging to the public of one large region, derived from telegraphy elsewhere, with later Indian networks as successors; implies tier 2, below reviewed tier 1.

why: The East India Company government wanted fast communication to administer and defend a large territory, and adapted electric telegraphy already in use in Britain and elsewhere.

date.basis: Evidence for this dated community entry; not necessarily the first possible use.

events.statement: Public use began and people used telegraph offices.
events.caveats: The source describes public opening and people using offices; individual class and regional barriers remain unassessed. See separate retrospective 1855 inland tariff event.

evidence.supports: Public use began and people used telegraph offices.

contributions.group: Members of the public using colonial Indian telegraph offices
contributions.resource: Sought to send messages when the service opened to public use.

evidence.supports: The abstract says the service opened for public use on 1 February 1855 and describes people rushing to telegraph offices to send messages.

date.label: February 1855
date.basis: Start month in later government statistical tariff table.

events.statement: A later colonial statistical publication reports an inland tariff of one rupee for sixteen words per 400 miles of telegraph line from February 1855.
events.scope: Inland telegraph tariff; historical terms, not a measured individual payment.
events.caveats: The historical tariff table does not establish affordability, language eligibility, number of customers or terms for all international messages. It reports a revision from April 1859.

evidence.locator: X Telegraph, tariff for inland telegrams
evidence.supports: The retrospective official table gives rate, unit and initial month.

earliest_record.rationale: Use and public opening are documented, while the military-administrative origins do not establish public access. Abstract only; individual class, regional and price barriers remain unassessed.

caveats: Public access was constrained by local availability and cost; degree of affordability, eligibility and actual reach remain unassessed.

research.note: Proposed distinct configuration and community entry; requires independent review. Independent review could not retrieve the full 1903 statistical source; tariff and related measure remain sourced pending direct verification.

measures.subject: Colonial Indian inland telegraph tariff
measures.conditions: Per sixteen words per 400 miles of telegraph line, from February 1855 according to 1903 retrospective table; not an individual transaction.

evidence.locator: X Telegraph, tariff for inland telegrams
evidence.supports: One rupee for sixteen words per 400 miles of line.
